claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets arise from variations in local lattice distortion.
Mechanical-property differences among these alloys arise from variations in short-range chemical order.
Local lattice distortion and short-range chemical order modify dislocation mobility during deformation.
Standard thermomechanical treatment can produce a single-phase FCC equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy.
Aging near 650°C for varied durations can systematically vary short-range chemical order in the selected alloys.
Aging near 650°C may enhance local lattice distortion in the selected alloys.
The number and identity of alloy constituents affect the local chemical environment.
Changes in short-range order alter stress fields around dislocation cores.
Changes in local lattice distortion alter stress fields around dislocation cores.
Altered stress fields around dislocation cores modify dislocation mobility.
Greater local lattice distortion produces more effective dislocation pinning.
Greater short-range chemical order produces more effective dislocation pinning.
More effective dislocation pinning increases yield strength.
More effective dislocation pinning may reduce ductility.
Alloys with greater measured lattice distortion or short-range order will have higher strength than the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline.
Alloys with greater measured lattice distortion or short-range order may have lower ductility than the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline.
The proposed relationship is limited to single-phase FCC alloys under conditions that avoid phase separation and secondary-phase formation.
Precipitation, segregation, or other competing mechanisms may overshadow effects attributed to local lattice distortion and short-range order.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that samples receive identical aging treatments, whereas the intervention and falsification design require aging treatments of varied duration. Fabrication and temperature may be identical, but aging duration is explicitly not identical.
